# Critique and Thirty Improvements

1. Do not mistake more outlines for realism; add planes, joints, overlap, and material cues.
2. Keep neutral identity separate from acting.
3. Prevent facial detail from becoming noise at 180×300.
4. Give ears and jaw different visibility by view.
5. Preserve eye readability during extreme close-ups and profiles.
6. Make lips change clearly across visemes.
7. Use elbows so gestures do not resemble rubber lines.
8. Use knees so running and crouching have believable weight.
9. Plant feet during stops and catches.
10. Keep crossed arms and pocket contact locked.
11. Attach carried props to the correct wrist side.
12. Separate world objects from hand props.
13. Use object materials: ceramic, metal, paper, glass, plastic, fabric, wood.
14. Add object shadows and highlights.
15. Give the office three depth layers.
16. Let camera parallax affect world objects consistently.
17. Make text bubbles point toward the speaker.
18. Move bubbles away from faces and title-safe regions.
19. Wrap dialogue instead of shrinking it into illegibility.
20. Keep every dialogue line within its authored timing.
21. Use insert shots for mug, machine display, spoon, and printer output.
22. Use an overhead shot to make the mug negotiation spatially clear.
23. Use a Dutch angle only at the machine malfunction.
24. Use slow push and whip-pan motion for escalation.
25. Use a stable final group tableau for the punchline.
26. Ensure objects persist in the source project and package.
27. Ensure preview and final export use identical evaluated object state.
28. Add tests that compare object hashes across action phases.
29. Add tests for jointed-limb geometry and anchored-bubble placement.
30. Reject completion if any proof frame is blank, clipped, symbolically crude, or visually repetitive.

## Revised insight

The prior short proved completeness, but this pass must prove cinematic density. The central improvement is not merely a different script; it is a reusable production layer where believable bodies and constructed objects share one camera, one timeline, one persistence contract, and one export path.
